title: slice-prioritization-eval-for-batchcache-configs
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: Produce a slice-aware evaluation and monitoring artifact that quantifies the latency vs quality tradeoffs across candidate batch/cache configurations, and surface a prioritized list of risky slices to drive canary rollouts and automated guardrails. Unlike prior broad LQ sweeps, this ticket designs a weighted slice-prioritization scheme that combines observed traffic importance, slice sensitivity (delta LQ under config perturbations), and business impact to rank slices for targeted regression detection and focused remediation.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible evaluation pipeline (eval-harness job) that runs candidate config diffs and produces per-slice latency and quality delta tables
A slice-priority score computed for each slice combining traffic share, sensitivity, and customer impact; exported as a CSV and visible in the dashboard
Defined canary thresholds and automated alerts: when top-10 slices exceed regression thresholds, a canary flag is raised and Rollback playbook is executed
Playbook for rolling canaries that includes exact metric thresholds, minimum sample sizes, and safe rollback criteria
Experiment notebooks and run artifacts uploaded to Drive with links in ticket
One internal demo to runtime and SRE with sample results for at least three config candidates (e.g., larger microbatch, increased KV TTL, aggressive eviction)
Cross-team review (PM + Design + SRE) sign-off recorded in comments
experiment_plan: Define slice taxonomy: user-intent buckets (instruction, summarization, code), prompt-length buckets (short/medium/long), high-cost customers, and rare but critical templates (legal/medical)
Assemble eval corpus: union of production-sampled prompts (anonymized), synthetic edge cases, and regression prompt suites from ops (target ~50k requests spread across slices)
Candidate config diffs: baseline (current prod), config-A (microbatch increase + small packing), config-B (aggressive KV TTL increase), config-C (pack+ttl combo with eviction bias)

For each config, run distributed eval-harness producing per-request latency p50/p95/p99, token throughput, model output, and quality annotations (automated similarity + targeted human labeling for top-1000 examples)
Compute per-slice deltas: delta_latency = cfg_latency - baseline_latency, delta_quality = baseline_quality - cfg_quality (so positive delta_quality is regression)
Compute slice_priority_score = w1 * traffic_share_rank + w2 * sensitivity_rank + w3 * customer_impact_rank; tune weights w1,w2,w3 in initial sweep and record final values
Run bootstrap confidence intervals per-slice and estimate minimum sample size needed to detect 1% absolute quality drop with 80% power
Ship artifacts (CSV, notebook, dashboard) and configure alert rules in Console for top-N slices
dataset_and_tools: Labeling queue: LabelStudio instance (project: slice-prio-1005) for human annotation
Dashboards: Grafana board 'LQ Slice Prioritization' and Console alert channel 'slice-regressions'
Statistical libraries: ArviZ + SciPy bootstrap helpers; internal LQ scoring toolkit
metrics_and_thresholds: Latency: keep delta_p50 <= 12ms for top-traffic slices; delta_p99 <= 60ms for high-SLA customers
Quality: absolute drop in task-level accuracy <= 0.5% for high-importance slices, <= 1.5% for general slices
Semantic similarity (embedding cosine): mean delta_cosine >= -0.01 tolerated; < -0.02 triggers alert
Hallucination proxy rate (model assertiveness): increase > 0.8% triggers P1 investigation
Minimum sample sizes: require >= 500 requests in a slice for automated alerting; for smaller slices require manual review
Slice priority alert: top-10 prioritized slices with combined priority score > 0.7 and any quality regression above thresholds will start canary rollback flow
runbook_and_rollout: Canary stage 1: 1% traffic to config candidate for 3 hours. Monitor top-10 slices and global metrics. If any slice exceeds thresholds, proceed to rollback immediately.
Canary stage 2: 5% traffic for 12 hours if stage 1 passes. Run human spot-checks on top-200 examples per top-3 slices.
Rollback criteria: any single high-priority slice with quality drop > threshold OR p99 latency spike > threshold for high-SLA tenant triggers instant rollback
Escalation: on rollback, create postmortem ticket and notify SRE/PM/Research. Capture minimal repro and diff artifacts for root cause analysis
Post-rollout monitoring: run slice-prio evaluation at 24h and 72h after rollout to detect slow regressions
Automation: plan to wire alerts to the runtime canary automation to pause traffic and revert to baseline image if thresholds hit
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created by Asha. Kickoff with runtime and eval teams. Initial slice taxonomy proposed.
2026-03-11: Assembled anonymized traffic sample (approx 52k requests). Spiked underrepresented legal/medical templates to ensure coverage.

2026-03-12: Implemented per-slice delta computation in eval-harness (PR 412). Early smoke runs completed for config-A; observed modest p50 improvements but a few high-cost slices showed quality drift.
2026-03-13: Human labeling batch kicked off for 1k examples across top-5 sensitive slices (LabelStudio). Estimated labels complete by 2026-03-16.

2026-03-14: Initial sensitivity ranking computed. Preliminary weights w1=0.5, w2=0.35, w3=0.15 chosen to favor traffic share but still surface sensitive low-volume slices. Meeting scheduled with PM and SRE 2026-03-15 for sign-off on canary thresholds.
Blockers: need updated access to some high-SLA tenant sample sets (request filed with Data Security), human labeling throughput currently limited; exploring contractor pool.
Next steps: finish labeling, run full candidate sweep for config-B/C, produce dashboard and CSV export, demo results to runtime+SRE by 2026-03-22
